newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-O'MEARA MAKES BUICK INVITATIONAL SECOND STRAIGHT WIN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-O'MEARA MAKES BUICK INVITATIONAL SECOND STRAIGHT WIN.

text.p: Mark O'Meara closed with a three-under par 33 on the back nine of the South Course at Torrey Pines Sunday to hold off Craig Stadler and win the Buick Invitational, his second straight victory.
O'Meara, who won the AT&T Pebble Beach National Pro-Am the week before, broke out of a tie with Stadler by making a 15-foot birdie putt at the 17th hole.
The victory was the 14th of his career. He earned $270,000, running his season total to a Tour-high $710,460.
"This victory was really special," the 40-year-old O'Meara said.

"I really didn't play the most sterling golf. I didn't stand on any tee and think I was going to stripe it down the middle. But I was standing on the ninth tee and decided in my mind that if I tried to dig a little bit deeper I might have a chance."
The round turned for O'Meara at the par-five 13th hole, when he hit a four-wood second shot to 22 feet left of the hole then made the eagle putt to go from one shot down to one ahead.
"I hit it perfect," he said, "right where it needed to go, pin-high left. That was totally a key out there."
O'Meara finished at 13-under par 275, two strokes ahead of seven players: David Ogrin, Duffy Waldorf, Donnie Hammond, Lee Janzen, Sweden's Jesper Parnevik, Stadler and Mike Hulbert.

Stadler needed a birdie at the par-five 18th hole to have a chance to tie. But his second shot wound up in deep rough short and right of the hole. His chip shot came up short of the green, leading to a bogey.
"In summation, it was a pretty pitiful effort," Stadler said. "I drove the ball really well today. But the better I drove it the worse I hit my iron shot."
Parnevik has now finished third, second, a tie for fifth and a tie for second in his four PGA Tour starts this year.
